newsitem.title: GREECE: Albanian army moves on town, four injured - Greek TV.
newsitem.headline: Albanian army moves on town, four injured - Greek TV.

text.p: The Albanian army was battling local insurgents near the southern Albanian port of Sarande on Wednesday and at least four people had been wounded, a Greek reporter at the scene said by telephone.

The reporter for the Greek Skai channel said that several truckloads of Albanian soldiers had taken up positions near the village of Styari, 10 km (six miles) east of Sarande, and were fighting armed locals.

Former Sarande prefect Dimitris Stefos also told Skai live by telephone that reports had reached the port of army deployments near Styari and Delvine, further east. Civilians had rushed to the scene from Sarande to join the local insurgents.
"A messenger has just returned and said there was fighting between locals and the army, and that there were wounded but we have no other details," he said.
Anti-government riots swept Sarande and surrounding towns over the weekend. Security forces abandoned the area and there has been widespread looting and burning of public buildings.
